criteria.reasoning: The memo opens with "Gerry Halvorsen died at home on Thursday, August 27, 2026," cites the obituary and the probate notice, and says the September 29 visit cannot go ahead as a solicitation. It does not treat him as living. It also mentions September 1 only as the obituary's publication date, not as the date of death.

The memo says "The September 29 visit cannot go ahead as a solicitation. The gallery proposal is not to be presented to Peg or anyone in the family." Action 1 cancels the 9/29 visit action. Action 4 allows only a condolence visit with no gift, proposal, pledge or estate matter and no proposal or rendering brought. If Peg raises the gallery, Ruth listens and tells Janet the same day. Section 4 bars proposing the gallery as a memorial naming. All of this matches the criterion.

Action #1 says to "Close proposal PR-2026-044 as 'Closed — donor deceased' (not transferred to Peg or anyone else)". It does not keep the proposal open, put it on hold, or reassign it to anyone. The memo also says the gallery proposal is not to be presented to the family before the bereavement period ends.

Action 1 says to "Mark record 10388 deceased, date of death 2026-08-27" and to "Remove Gerry from all appeals, mailings, e-mail lists and event invitations." Action 2 says to "Remove Gerry from the Fall Appeal before the mail file goes to the printer on 2026-09-28." This covers the deceased update with the date of death, the general suppression, and the Fall Appeal.

The memo gives the solicitation bar as "before February 28, 2027," counted from the obituary's September 1 publication ("180 days after the death was confirmed by the obituary of 2026-09-01"). The criterion requires 2027-02-23, and names 2027-02-28 as a failing date.

The memo's action 2 says to "Re-address the household's Fall Appeal letter to Mrs. Margaret Halvorsen alone, at the same ask string," which keeps Margaret on the appeal. Action 3 adds "Annual appeals continue as normal" for Peg, Kristin and Erik, so Kristin also stays on the appeal. The criterion explicitly fails a memo that re-addresses the household letter to Margaret alone or leaves either of them on the Fall Appeal.

Action 6 recommends that Ruth send the Halvorsen Family Foundation letter of request by October 15 as planned ($15,000), and describes it as a routine renewal rather than a personal ask. That is the exact FAIL condition: recommending the October 15 letter before the bereavement period ends and treating the foundation as outside the no-solicitation rule.
The memo states "Unpaid balance: $80,000" and refers the $80,000 balance to the CFO. The criterion requires $70,000 and names $80,000 as a failing figure, since it misses the $10,000 paid 2026-06-12.

Action 7 refers the $80,000 balance to CFO Denise Okafor and says "Only Denise decides whether to present a claim and deals with the estate about the pledge. No one in development asks Peg, Erik, Kristin or the family foundation to pay it, and no pledge reminder goes to the household." Section 4 adds a bar on discussing the pledge or estate with any family member, including Erik as personal representative. Ruth's only role is the internal referral, and the foundation letter is told not to mention the pledge. None of the FAIL conditions appear.

Action #7, the pledge referral to CFO Denise Okafor, includes "probate case 2026PR000214, personal representative **Erik T. Halvorsen** (attorney Laura Vang, Vang & Steinke, S.C.), and the **claims deadline of 2026-12-28**." This gives the required deadline and names the correct personal representative. Nothing elsewhere in the memo contradicts either point.

Action 8 reads: "Notify Samuel Achterberg of the $100,000 bequest intention. He alone contacts the personal representative or the estate's attorney to learn whether the will includes a gift to the Center." That routes the bequest to the Director of Planned Giving as the sole contact. Section 4 bars discussing the bequest or estate with any family member. Ruth only notifies Achterberg and does not contact the family or the estate herself. The memo does not give Achterberg's title, but he is named and clearly handles planned giving, which is enough.

Action 8 says: "Keep it as an expectancy: it is not booked as revenue, a receivable or campaign credit until the estate's distribution is received." That matches the criterion's required treatment. The memo also notes that it is unknown whether the probated will still contains the bequest, and nowhere states that the estate owes or will pay $100,000.

Action 5 has the condolence letter prepared by Nadia Ferris and signed by President & CEO Laurel Whitfield. It does not mention the Board Chair, Thomas Brandvold, as a co-signer. The criterion fails a letter signed by the CEO alone.

The memo addresses memorial gifts in two places. It notes that three memorial gifts have arrived and that the obituary directs memorials to the arts education programs. Action 9 says to "send Peg a monthly list of memorial donors' names and addresses, never the amounts." This matches the criterion, and the memo does not propose telling the family the amounts or a total.

The facts the memo states about Gerry, his family, the estate, his gifts and the foundation all trace to the files. These include the August 27 death at home, the survivors, case 2026PR000214, Erik as personal representative, attorney Laura Vang, the December 28 claims deadline, the 2021 letter of intent, the foundation trustees and the three memorial gifts. It gives no cause of death and no estate value. It says the bequest rests on the 2021 letter and that "We do not know whether the will admitted to probate still contains it," so it does not assert that the current will contains it. The $80,000 balance is an arithmetic or superseded-figure issue for other criteria. The staff names (Holly Prochaska, Nadia Ferris, Denise Okafor) are not in the files I could see, but they most likely come from the policy and mail files that were not shown, so I found no unsupported fact.
